sq: Më 15 qershor 1389, në Fushën e Kosovës, ushtria osmane e Sulltan Muratit I u ndesh me një koalicion fisnikësh ballkanikë, të prirë nga Knez Lazari i Serbisë, me trupa nga Bosnja.
Sipas kronikës së familjes shqiptare Muzaka, aty luftuan edhe fisnikë shqiptarë, dhe Teodor Muzaka II ra në betejë.
U vranë edhe Lazari, edhe Murati: sulltanin e goditi për vdekje një kalorës i krishterë.
Sipas traditës shqiptare, kalorësi ishte Millosh Kopiliqi.
Asnjëra palë nuk fitoi qartë, por përparimi osman në Ballkan vazhdoi.
en: On 15 June 1389, on the plain of Kosovo, the Ottoman army of Sultan Murad I met a coalition of Balkan lords led by Prince Lazar of Serbia, with troops from Bosnia.
According to the chronicle of the Albanian Muzaka family, Albanian lords fought there too, and Teodor Muzaka II fell in the battle.
Both Lazar and Murad were killed: the Sultan was struck down by a Christian knight.
In Albanian tradition, the knight was Millosh Kopiliqi.
Neither side won outright, but the Ottoman advance into the Balkans went on.

sources.title: Calendar note
sources.note: The battle was fought on 15 June 1389 in the Julian calendar then in use. It is commemorated on 28 June because the Serbian Orthodox Church still uses the Julian calendar, which today runs 13 days behind.

sources.title: The knight
sources.note: Serbian tradition names him Miloš Obilić (earlier Kobilić); Albanian tradition, Millosh Kopiliqi. Both names appear only in later sources.
